item.title: 1972: Pirates Release Bill Mazeroski, 36, Hall of Famer
item.description: The notable playing careers of two National League infielders end today when the Pittsburgh Pirates unconditionally release second baseman, 1960 World Series hero and future Hall of Famer Bill Mazeroski, 36, and the Los Angeles Dodgers release shortstop, 1962 NL MVP and record-setting base-stealer Maury Wills, 40. Photo: arthur.wessel (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2021: Prieto Hired as Rays First Base Coach
item.description: On October 24, 2021, Prieto was hired as the first base coach for the Tampa Bay Rays. Photo: Ken Lund from Reno, Nevada, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2019: Cubs Hire Ross as Manager, Replacing Joe Maddon
item.description: On October 24, 2019, the Cubs hired Ross as their manager to replace Joe Maddon, signing him to a three-year contract. Photo: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Zachary D. (Public domain).

item.title: 2018: Price Holds Dodgers to Two Runs, Red Sox Lead 2-0
item.description: David Price held the Los Angeles Dodgers to two runs and three hits over six innings, as the Boston Red Sox won Game 2 at Fenway Park, 4–2, and took a 2–0 lead in the World Series prior to heading to Dodger Stadium for the next game. For the second consecutive game, J. D. Martinez drove in the go-ahead run with a two-run single in the fifth inning that provided the winning margin. Photo: Arturo Pardavila III from Hoboken, NJ, USA (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2018: Benny Valenzuela, 85, Mexican Third Baseman
item.description: Benny Valenzuela, 85, Mexican third baseman who played for the 1958 St. Louis Cardinals.

item.title: 2017: Clayton Kershaw Leads Dodgers Past Astros 3-1 in Game 1
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers won Game 1 of the World Series over the Houston Astros at Dodger Stadium, 3–1, behind solid pitching by Clayton Kershaw to take a 1–0 series lead. Photo: Christopher Okula (Original version) UCinternational (Crop) (Public domain).

item.title: 2015: Rays Hire Matt Quatraro as Third Base Coach
item.description: On October 24, 2015, the Rays hired Matt Quatraro as their new third base coach and Montoyo became the bench coach, replacing Tom Foley. Photo: Keith Allison from Hanover, MD, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2012: Giants Sweep Tigers in World Series Starting Oct. 24
item.description: With the win, the National League champion earned home field advantage for the World Series, which began on October 24, 2012 and ended on October 28, 2012 when the San Francisco Giants swept the Detroit Tigers. Photo: Michael Marconi (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2012: Pablo Sandoval Hits Three Homers in Giants' Game 1 Win
item.description: Pablo Sandoval of the San Francisco Giants becomes the fourth player in major league history to hit three home runs in a World Series game, hitting two of them off Justin Verlander of the Detroit Tigers. The Giants go on to defeat the Tigers 8–3 at AT&T Park in Game 1. Photo: mvmarconi on Flickr (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2007: Hall of Fame to Honor Buck O'Neil With Lifetime Award
item.description: The National Baseball Hall of Fame announces that it will honor Buck O'Neil by establishing a lifetime achievement award in his name. O'Neil, a Negro league first baseman and manager who died in October 2006, will be honored with a statue to be dedicated at the next Hall of Fame induction in Cooperstown, N.Y. After leaving the Negro leagues, O'Neil became the first African American coach in the majors by joining the… Photo: kc congdon from rochester, ny (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2004: Red Sox Beat Fenway 6-2 Behind Curt Schilling, Take 2-0 Lead
item.description: The Red Sox win 6-2 at Fenway Park behind Curt Schilling, to take the Series lead 2-0. Schilling goes 6 innings, giving up only 1 run (not earned) and only 4 hits, while striking out 4. Photo: User Googie man on en.wikipedia (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1996: Andy Pettitte Outduels Smoltz, Yankees Win Game 5 1-0
item.description: In Game 5 of the 1996 World Series, the Atlanta Braves play their final game at Fulton County Stadium vs. the New York Yankees. Andy Pettitte outduels eventual NL Cy Young winner John Smoltz as the Yankees win Game 5 1-0 to take a 3-2 series lead. Photo: Keith Allison on Flickr. Cropped by User:Staxringold. (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1992: Blue Jays Beat Braves 4-3, Clinch First World Series Title
item.description: The Toronto Blue Jays clinch their first World Series championship with a 4–3 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 6. Dave Winfield's 2–out, 2–run double in the top of the 11th gives Toronto a 4–2 lead. The Braves score one run in the bottom half of the inning and have the tying run on the 3rd when the final out is made. Jimmy Key wins the game in relief, and Candy Maldonado homers for Toronto. Photo: Erik Drost (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1992: Blue Jays Become First Non-U.S. Team to Win World Series
item.description: The Toronto Blue Jays become the first Major League Baseball team based outside the United States to win the World Series. Photo: Erik Drost (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1985: Danny Jackson Throws Immaculate Inning in World Series Game 5
item.description: Kansas City Royals pitcher Danny Jackson throws an "Immaculate Inning" in Game 5 of the World Series, the first such inning in the Fall Classic's 82-year history. Jackson needs just nine pitches to retire Cardinals hitters Terry Pendleton, who fans, Tom Nieto, who's caught looking, and Brian Harper, who also strikes out swinging.

item.title: 1980: Whitey Herzog to Manage and Run Cardinals in 1981
item.description: The St. Louis Cardinals announce that newly appointed general manager Whitey Herzog will return to the Redbird dugout and serve as both manager and GM for the 1981 season. Herzog had temporarily surrendered the former job August 29 to interim pilot Red Schoendienst when he was appointed head of the club's baseball operations department. Photo: Johnmaxmena, John Mena (CC BY 3.0).

item.title: 1977: Red Sox Owner Jean Yawkey Fires Dick O'Connell
item.description: Boston Red Sox owner Jean R. Yawkey fires two-time The Sporting News Executive of the Year Dick O'Connell and his top lieutenants to clear the way for Haywood Sullivan, named general manager, and Buddy LeRoux, named executive vice president/administration. Sullivan and LeRoux are the general partners of a new ownership group expected to take control of the team in the coming days.

item.title: 1975: Astros Acquire Joaquín Andújar From Reds for Two Players
item.description: The rebuilding Houston Astros acquire 22-year-old pitching prospect Joaquín Andújar from the world-champion Reds for two "players to be named later", minor-leaguers Carlos Alfonso and Luis Sánchez. Andújar will begin his colorful, 13-year MLB career in 1976 by winning a spot in Houston's starting rotation. Photo: Ted Rozumalski (Public domain).

item.title: 1974: Billy Martin Named AP American League Manager of the Year
item.description: Billy Martin is named the Associated Press American League Manager of the Year after leading his Texas Rangers to a second-place finish in the AL West.

item.title: 1973: Al Brazle, 60, Pitcher Who Won 97 Games for Cardinals
item.description: Al Brazle, 60, pitcher who won 97 games for the St. Louis Cardinals (1943 and 1946–1954), also leading the NL in saves twice; 1946 World Series champion.

item.title: 1973: Red Sox Swap Pitchers, Send Marty Pattin to Royals for Dick Drago
item.description: The Red Sox continue what will be an extremely active off-season for them by exchanging right-handed pitchers with the Kansas City Royals, sending Marty Pattin to the Royals for Dick Drago.

item.title: 1972: Jackie Robinson, 53, Hall of Fame Second Baseman for Dodgers
item.description: Jackie Robinson, 53, Hall of Fame second baseman for the Brooklyn Dodgers who broke Major League Baseball's color line in 1947 after beginning his professional career for the Kansas City Monarchs of the Negro American League; batted .311 in his ten-year National League career, leading the NL in batting average (.342) in 1949; also led his league in stolen bases in 1947 and 1949; 1947 Major League Rookie of the Year…

item.title: 1970: Andy Oyler, 90, Infielder-Outfielder for 1902 Baltimore Orioles
item.description: Andy Oyler, 90, infielder–outfielder in 27 games for the 1902 Baltimore Orioles.

item.title: 1962: Hiram Bithorn Stadium Opens in San Juan, Puerto Rico
item.description: The Hiram Bithorn Stadium was opened on October 24, 1962 in San Juan, Puerto Rico. Photo: Mtmelendez (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1959: Braves Sign Rico Carty as Amateur Free Agent
item.description: October 24, 1959: Rico Carty was signed as an amateur free agent by the Braves.

item.title: 1956: Birdie Tebbetts Named MLB Manager of the Year by Sporting News
item.description: The Sporting News names Birdie Tebbetts MLB Manager of the Year. Tebbetts' 1956 Cincinnati Redlegs improved by 16 games over 1955's edition and missed the National League pennant by only two games.

item.title: 1951: Senators Send Willy Miranda to White Sox for Floyd Baker
item.description: The Washington Senators send slick-fielding shortstop Willy Miranda to the Chicago White Sox for veteran infielder Floyd Baker.

item.title: 1947: Indians Release Mel Harder, Who Stays on as Pitching Coach
item.description: The Cleveland Indians release pitcher Mel Harder, a 20-year veteran who won 223 games in a Cleveland uniform. He remains with the club as its pitching coach.

item.title: 1946: Yankees Trade Tiny Bonham to Pirates for Cookie Cuccurullo
item.description: The New York Yankees trade right-hander Tiny Bonham to the Pittsburgh Pirates for southpaw Cookie Cuccurullo. Bonham, 33, won 21 games for the 1942 Yankees but slumped to a 5–8 (3.70) mark in 18 games for the 1946 Bombers. Photo: Unknown (Public domain).

item.title: 1908: Billy Murray Introduces Take Me Out to the Ball Game
item.description: "Take Me Out to the Ball Game" is introduced by singer Billy Murray. The songwriting team of Albert Von Tilzer (music) and Jack Norworth (lyrics) who created the immortal tune have never seen a game. Over the past 100 years, more than 400 musicians from every conceivable genre have recorded the song.

item.title: 1892: Beaneaters Win Fifth Straight Over Spiders to Capture Title
item.description: The Beaneaters win their fifth consecutive game over the Spiders to capture the championship.

item.title: 1888: Browns Score Four in Eighth, Beat Giants 7-5
item.description: The Browns get a must-win by scoring four runs in the eighth to beat the Giants 7–5. Photo: J Wood, 208 Bowery, N.Y. (Public domain).

item.title: 1884: Providence Grays Beat New York Metropolitans 3-1 in Darkness-Shortened Game
item.description: The Providence Grays take the 2nd game of the best of 3 series against the New York Metropolitans by a score of 3–1. The game at the Polo Grounds is called after 7 innings because of darkness. (World Series results are also recorded for 1885.) Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1879: Cincinnati Reds Formally Withdraw From National League
item.description: The Cincinnati Reds formally withdraw from the National League.
